deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page (folio 4r, archival pagination '7.', circled '4'). It is philosophical draft text belonging to Riemann's natural-philosophy fragments. In the published Gesammelte Werke (Weber/Dedekind, 1876/1892) this material appears among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts', under 'Naturphilosophie'. The page has three parts.

(a) Section heading '2. Vergleichung dieser Naturauffassung mit der Naturauffassung Herbarts' (comparison of this conception of nature with Herbart's). It follows the preceding pages, where motion is derived from the minimisation of potentials: the gravitational potential P = g∬dm dm'/r, the Poisson equation ΔV = -4πρ, and a Dirichlet-type variational characterisation of V. The key thesis here is that Herbart's 'beziehungslos Gesetzte' (absolutely posited being, his 'Reale') should be identified not with the chemical atoms but with 'das dem Raum zu Grunde liegende Reale', the real that underlies space. This is Riemann's field or aether ontology set against Herbartian monadology. Three fragments follow, separated by gaps ('Lücke'):
- 'ferner ... werden diese Causalbegriffe durch die Erfahrung bestätigt' (these causal concepts are confirmed by experience);
- '1) Ist es wahrscheinlich, dass alle Wirkungen in die Ferne mittelbare Wirkungen seien?' (is it probable that all actions at a distance are mediated actions?). This is a programmatic question about contiguous action versus action at a distance, consistent with the previous page's remark that gravitation can be reduced to forces between neighbouring space elements.

(b) 'Blatt 5': the title 'Versuch einer Lehre von den Grundbegriffen der Mathematik und Physik, als Grundlage für die Naturerklärung'. It opens with the definition 'Naturwissenschaft ist der Versuch, die Natur durch genaue Begriffe aufzufassen' (natural science is the attempt to grasp nature through exact concepts). A bracketed elaboration says that the concepts complete present perceptions and predetermine future ones as necessary. A footnote (+) stresses why the origin of concepts must be traced: only thus can their meaning be fixed adequately for explaining nature. It then poses the first question to investigate: how are concepts formed, insofar as this is observable, i.e. by what path does natural science advance?

(c) 'Blatt 6': a second, revised fair copy of the same title and opening sentence, continued on the next page. The continuation describes concept systems revised when unexpected or improbable observations occur, with 'explanation' defined as the completion or correction of the concept system. It then turns to Herbart's derivation of the categories from experience, as opposed to Kant's a priori categories.

No formulas, computations or mathematical steps appear on this page.

results.what: Programme for a theory of the basic concepts of mathematics and physics. Natural science is defined as grasping nature through exact concepts, and concept systems are revised when predictions fail (an early hypothetico-deductive or falsificationist epistemology, framed against Herbart and Kant).
results.modern_name: Hypothetico-deductive account of scientific concept formation / theory change
results.usually_credited_to: Various 19th–20th c. philosophers of science (e.g. Whewell, Mach, later Popper); Riemann's fragment published 1876 in Gesammelte Werke

results.what: Identification of Herbart's 'Reale' with what underlies space rather than with chemical atoms. Question whether all action at a distance is mediated (contiguous action).
results.modern_name: Field/aether ontology; contiguous action (Nahwirkung) versus action at a distance
results.usually_credited_to: Faraday/Maxwell for field physics; Riemann's own aether speculations are in the published 'Naturphilosophie' fragments

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely philosophical draft text that was already edited and published by Dedekind and Weber in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (Naturphilosophie fragments, 'Versuch einer Lehre von den Grundbegriffen...'). It contains no mathematics, and its content is well known in the Riemann and Herbart literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Gesetzte' is written as a superscript over 'Seiende'. The intended reading is 'Das beziehungslos Gesetzte (Seiende)', not an insertion replacing a word.

The fragment 'Ferner weil werden diese Causalbegriffe ...' is grammatically odd. The image reading of the first words is uncertain (possibly 'Ferner weil' followed by an incomplete or altered clause), so it should be flagged as uncertain.
The struck bracketed word after 'als nothwendig' in the Blatt 5 passage is faint pencil/crossed and plausibly reads 'vorherbestimmt'. It should be kept as uncertain.

Marginalia omitted by the machine transcription: a pencil cross mark beside the Blatt 5 header area, a pencil 'Anm' (Anmerkung) beside the footnote, and a pencil archival note at right, roughly 'Naturphilosophie 1.'. There are also pencil vertical strokes and tally marks in the right margin near the bottom.

In the Blatt 6 text, the insertion over 'Begriffen' reads 'durch welche wir die Natur auffassen, werden'. The corrected sentence is 'Nach den Begriffen, durch welche wir die Natur auffassen, werden nicht bloss ...', matching the Blatt 5 version.
